meeting_header: Date: 2026-02-12; Start: 16:00 UTC; Duration: 55min; Attendees: Samir Patel, Eloise Cheng (Redwood) — Dr. Maya Rios, Tom Becker, Leila Ortiz (Aurora Therapeutics)
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review latest bench runs comparing Redwood's inference stack vs Aurora's incumbent provider. Main focus: p99 latency regressions under batching, routing policy impact when fallback triggers, quantization quality tradeoffs. Agreed on next steps to run synthetic replay and try two quantization profiles. Follow-up stress window to be scheduled.
topics: Routing policy behavior under partial capacity (fallbacks)
Quantization profiles: 8-bit vs 4-bit tradeoffs and cleanliness of outputs
KV/prefix cache effectiveness and cache warmup
Dedicated slots vs hosted burst for steady throughput
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 55 minutes today, um quick roll call?
[00:07] Maya: yeah Maya here. Tom here, Leila here.
[00:10] Samir: great, Eloise?
[00:12] Eloise: Eloise on the call. hi all. quick agenda: bench numbers, routing, quantization notes, next steps.
[00:20] Maya: sounds good, just wanna make sure we cover the p99 spikes we saw yesterday.
[00:25] Tom: yep we replayed a small sample, baseline (IncumbentCloud) was showing p50 ~90ms p95 ~180ms p99 ~420ms for our 1k token prompt distribution. Redwood run was p50 85ms p95 200ms p99 600ms — so p99 worse.
[00:45] Eloise: thanks for the numbers Tom, couple of clarifications: were those Redwood numbers with caching enabled and the 4-bit quantization profile or the 8-bit?
[00:52] Tom: that set was 4-bit q + prefix cache enabled but we had batching turned up to 8 because we wanted to match throughput.
[00:59] Eloise: okay that explains some of it — with aggressive batching and lower precision sometimes you see longer tail when cache misses align with large batches, especially on warmup.
[01:12] Leila: we definitely see warmup issues, first 10 minutes of the run are noisy. but even steady-state after 30 minutes we saw occasional 500-700ms p99s.
[01:23] Samir: understood. quick note: our routing policy in the test was set to prefer low-cost variants then fallback; that means under transient saturation some requests get routed to a slightly heavier model variant for correctness and that can inflate tails. we can tweak policy to prefer latency SLO instead.
[01:39] Maya: what are the tradeoffs if we prefer latency SLO? cost? quality?
[01:44] Eloise: preferring latency SLO will route to a higher‑throughput instance shape or a less-quantized model variant (8-bit) so cost goes up ~15-25% in our estimate, but p99 drops significantly. quality change depends — 8-bit usually has negligible quality delta compared to 4-bit for our models, but it's model dependent.
[02:00] Tom: can you share the exact numbers that produce the delta? we want to show our stakeholders a clear cost/latency table.
[02:05] Samir: yes, we'll share a small table. quick verbal: for this workload when switching from 4-bit+aggressive batching to 8-bit+batching=4, we saw p99 move from ~600ms to ~230ms, throughput stayed within 90% of target, cost estimate +18%.
[02:23] Maya: that's promising. can you explain the cache warmup impact? we saw big improvements after a few minutes.
[02:30] Eloise: sure — prefix/KV cache helps when prompts share prefixes (reused system prompts, common user queries). on first occurance of a new prefix the runtime must populate KV cache and optimiser paths, during that time tokens take longer. also when we change quantization or model variant you get cold caches. for steady-state we recommend a short priming run or synthetic replay.
[02:48] Leila: we can do a priming pass but want to understand how fast the cache recovers after a model failover or fallback.
[02:54] Eloise: typically cache repopulation is incremental; for our observed distribution the 95th percentile of cache repopulation was ~120s but p99 effects can last longer depending on distribution. we'll capture trace metrics in the replay.
[03:07] Tom: about routing — yesterday the fallback triggered to a heavier variant because one worker's GPU spiked. is there a way to isolate that single-worker jitter rather than failing the whole routing class?
[03:16] Eloise: yes we have per-pool health heuristics and progressive rollbacks, we can make fallback only apply to a subset of requests (canary routing). also we can set jitter thresholds so single worker spikes don't cause global fallback.
[03:28] Maya: would that add complexity on our side? we don't want to manage more knobs.
[03:32] Samir: Redwood can suggest a policy out of the box: latency-preferred, cost-balanced, or safe-fallback. we'll propose one tuned to Aurora's SLOs so minimal config on your end.
[03:43] Leila: can we talk about the quantization profiles Eloise mentioned? we care about hallucination risk for clinical notes. lower bit quantization sometimes causes odd tokenization differences.
[03:52] Eloise: absolutely — two profiles we're preparing: 1) conservative 8-bit (fast, safe) 2) aggressive 4-bit with per-layer exceptions for attention/embedding matrices to preserve quality. we'll run our internal evals and also the prompt set you provided to compute ROUGE/BLEU and a small human-in-the-loop check.
[04:12] Tom: will the aggressive profile still meet our throughput target?
[04:15] Eloise: yes but with slightly higher p99 variance as you saw. throughput nominally increases but tail worsens; it's a classic trade-off.
[04:22] Maya: given our clinical compliance, we prefer stable tails even if cost is a bit higher.
[04:26] Samir: noted — so action plan: produce two profiles, run replay on both and share perf+quality table.
[04:33] [05:00] (brief silence, background typing)
[05:10] Tom: a quick question: the baseline numbers are from our incumbent vendor with a dedicated instance pool; are we comparing like-for-like?
[05:18] Eloise: good call — the previous runs were compared to a dedicated baseline. for fairness, we can spin a dedicated Redwood pool for the stress run or we can match config to their dedicated instance types. cost comparisons will be annotated accordingly.
[05:31] Leila: firewall/VPC egress rules might affect latency to the Redwood private endpoint; we saw occasional 20-40ms variance based on route.
[05:39] Samir: please send exact egress rules — we can coordinate with infra to reduce hop count or add a regional endpoint.
[05:45] Maya: I also want to flag security questions — SOC2 and KMS integration. we've already reviewed the docs but can you confirm audit log granularity for model id and request-level metadata?
[05:56] Samir: yes audit logs include model id, route, token counts, and request id; we can push logs to your SIEM or S3 with retention options. KMS/HSM support is available for Private.
[06:06] Maya: great.
[06:08] Eloise: circling back to benchmarks — we have a proposed stress test next week. ask: can Aurora provide a 48-hour representative traffic trace? that helps recreate tail behavior reliably.
[06:17] Tom: yes we'll export from our telemetry and upload to the shared bucket.
[06:20] Samir: perfect. also we'll include a suggested config to test: dedicated 8-slot pool with latency-preferred routing + conservative 8-bit profile. then run aggressive 4-bit with batch 8 and show deltas.
[06:34] Leila: when you run the dedicated stress window, will you run with the same sequence distribution or randomize? we prefer sequence-preserving replay.
[06:40] Eloise: sequence preserving — exact ordering is important for cache warmup fidelity.
[06:45] Maya: one more ask: add a row to the perf table for cost per 1M tokens and ops per second so our procurement team can evaluate.
[06:53] Samir: sure we'll include cost per 1M tokens, avg token cost, and cost delta vs baseline.
[06:58] Tom: any concerns about model drift when switching quantization? are there regression detection hooks?
[07:03] Eloise: Redwood Optimize includes eval hooks; we can run prompt set before/after quantization and flag regressions above a threshold. we can also pin a fallback to the original model for a percentage of traffic.
[07:15] Maya: good.
[07:18] Samir: to close: action owners recap and dates. Eloise will produce quant profiles and perf table by 2026-02-16; Tom will upload trace by 2026-02-18; Leila will confirm SRE window and egress rules by 2026-02-19; schedule stress run week of 2026-02-23.
[07:36] Leila: sounds good.
[07:38] Maya: thanks all, this was helpful.
[07:41] Samir: thanks, we'll follow up with a short doc and calendar invite.
[07:44] (meeting ends)
notes: Transcript contains typical ASR errors: some product names transcribed differently in earlier runs. referenced artifacts: shared bucket link (s3://aurora-redwood-poc), perf spreadsheet (link sent after meeting).
